lawyer:
Mainul Hosein with Md Mozammel Huq and Manjur Kader, Md Iqbal Malik, Advocates -For the Accused-Appellants
Snigdha Huq, Assistant Attorney-General with Robiul Karim, Assistant Attorney-General -For the Respondent-State
parties:
Khairul @ Abul Kalam and another ------ Appellants
vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Tariqul Hakim J: This criminal appeal preferred by accused appellants Khairul alias Abul Kalam Sawdagor and Khokan Sawdagor is directed against the judgment and order dated 18-5-1995 passed by the Sessions Judge, Jhalokati in Sessions Case No. 11 of 1993 arising out of PS Case No. 3 dated 26-6-91 corresponding to GR No. 29 of 1991 convicting the accused appellants under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and sentencing them to suffer imprisonment for life and to pay a fine of Taka 2000 only, in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for one year more.

2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the complainant Harunur Rashid Khandkar (PW 3) on 25-6-91 at about 2 AM at night was awakened from his sleep on hearing his mother Suraton Bibi's shouting. Immediately he and his wife PW 8 came out of their but and in the moonlight saw the accused appellants running away with sharp cutting Dao in their hands; at the same time his brother PW 7 also came out of his but on hearing his mother's shouting who also saw the accused appellants running away and together went into their mother's room and found her with bleeding injury in the neck. Their mother Suraton Bibi reported to them that the accused appellants had inflicted the injury on her neck and subsequently she succumbed to her injuries. It was also claimed by the prosecution that the accused appellant No. 1 is the brother of the wife of PW 7 and accused appellant No. 2 is the cousin (Chachato Bhai) of appellant No. 1. It was further alleged by the prosecution that the deceased loved the children of the first wife of PW 7, which was not liked by the second wife of PW 7 and accordingly, there was a quarrel between the second wife and the deceased over the children which was reported by the second wife to the accused appellants who thereafter killed the deceased out of revenge. Accordingly, the informant (PW 3) lodged the first information report and the aforesaid police station case was started.

3. The police took up investigation, visited the place of occurrence, prepared sketch map with separate index, prepared inquest report, sent the body of the deceased to the morgue for post mortem examination, seized alamats by preparing seizure list and examined witnesses and recorded their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and finally, submitted charge sheet against the accused appellants as prima facie case was made out against them under sections 448/302/34 of the Penal Code.

4. The case record ultimately came to the file of the present trial Court who on the basis of materials available on record framed charge against the accused appellants under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code and read it out to the accused on dock to which they pleaded not guilty and demanded trial.

5. The prosecution examined 13 witnesses all of whom were cross-examined by the defence. After close of the prosecution witnesses the accused on dock were examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to which they repeated their innocence. The defence did not adduce any evidence. The defence case as could be gathered from the trend of cross-examination is total denial and their, inter alia, case is that the accused appellants have been falsely implicated in this case out of enmity and grudge.

6. The learned trial Court thereafter in consideration of the evidence on record as well as in the facts and circumstance of the case found the accused appellants guilty of the offence charged and convicted them thereunder and sentenced them for the aforesaid term as well as to pay fine with a default clause as mentioned above. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied thereby the accused appellants have come up with the present appeal which is opposed by the respondent-State through the learned Assistant Attorney-General Ms Snigdha Huq.

7. Mr Mainul Hosein, the learned Advocate for the accused appellants, took us through the first information report, charge-sheet, deposition of prosecution witnesses, impugned judgment and other material papers/documents as available in the paper book and submits that this is a case of no evidence, inasmuch as, the learned trial Court did not consider that the prosecution case was embellished by the prosecution stage by stage. He further submits that the learned trial Court ought to have acquitted the accused appellants on the ground that there is no eye-witness to prove the occurrence and also on the ground that the deceased's neck was cut to such an extent that she was unable to breath which indicates that she could not have made any statement to the prosecution witnesses by way of dying declaration as alleged by the prosecution. He further submits that the order of conviction and sentence was passed on the evidence of highly interested, partisan and tutored witnesses such as PWs 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 who were near relatives of the deceased and enemies of the accused appellants and, as such, the same is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the medical examination report clearly showed that the respiratory mechanism of the deceased's body was cut by the assailants and that it was impossible for her to disclose the names of the accused appellants to the prosecution witnesses and that fact not having been considered by the Trial Judge the accused appellants have been seriously prejudiced and accordingly, the impugned order of conviction and sentence should be set aside.

8. As against this, the learned Assistant Attorney-General Ms Snigdha Huq submits that the learned trial Court has rightly found the accused appellants guilty for the offence charged after considering all the evidence on record. She further submits that the medical report indicates that although the respiratory mechanism of the deceased's body was cut nevertheless there is no mentioning of the vocal cord of the deceased which indicates that despite the injury to the respiratory organ the deceased was able to speak and disclose the names of the assailants to the prosecution witnesses. Accordingly, the deceased's dying declaration was rightly admitted into evidence. She further submits that the prosecution witnesses and several inmates of the place of occurrence house saw the accused appellants with sharp cutting weapons leaving the place of occurrence house at the time of occurrence and there is no reason to disbelieve their evidence. She accordingly, submits that the impugned order of conviction and sentence calls for no interference by this Court.

9. PW 1, Sudhir Kumar Das and PW 2 Mafizur Rahman, two constables of Kathalia PS deposed about accompanying the body of the deceased to the morgue for post mortem examination on 27-6-91.

10. PW 3 Harun-ur-Rashid, (informant) deposed that at about 2-00 AM in the morning on the night of the occurrence (10th of Ashar) he was awakened from his sleep by the sound of shouting from his mother's room. He then came out of his room with his wife but before entering his mother's room they saw the accused appellants in the moonlight leaving the premises with Dao in his hand. He went inside his mother's room with his wife and found his mother was inflicted with bleeding injury on the left side of her neck. His brother Sultan had also come to his mother's room. Together they wrapped the injured part of the neck with a Gamcha. His mother then put her arms round the neck of his elder brother Sultan PW 7 and reported to him that the accused appellant Khairul and Khokon had inflicted the injuries on her. He further deposed that he heard these statements when his mother reported the same to his elder brother. His mother further said that she recognised the assailants from the light of hurricane in the room although at that time they did not find any hurricane there. Their mother succumbed to her injury half an hour later. On hearing their hue and cry Mozahar, Naren Mondal, Bilkis, Momin Khan and others came to the place of occurrence house. The children of PW 7 were also crying and one of them Kajal, PW 4, said that they recognised the accused appellants Khairul and Khokan and that the accused appellant Khairul had inflicted the blow. He further deposed that there would often be quarrels between the deceased and the second wife of PW 7 over the children of PW 7's first wife and one such quarrel also took place on the night prior to the occurrence and at that time the accused appellant No. 1 (Khairul) the brother of PW 7's second wife said “ইহার ব্যবস্থা আমি করব”. His father was not at home on the night of the occurrence and came there on the following morning. He filed the ejahar then. He went to the police station accompanied by the Chowkidar and a Member of the local Union Parishad and filed the ejahar. He proved the Ejahar as Exhibit 1 and his signature therein as Exhibit 1(1) He further deposed that the police investigated the case and seized alamats after preparing seizure list. The bamboo mat on which the deceased was sleeping was blood stained and seized by the police amongst other things along with deceased's saree and a pillow, which were also blood stained. He also proved the Gamcha with which the deceased's neck was wrapped as Exhibit 6. He further deposed that they were four brothers ie Sultan, Harun, Selim and Delwar all of whom were married, and one sister by the name Rahela. He further deposed that Selim, Delwar and Rahela were not witnesses in this case. He further deposed that Mozaffar PW 10 lived in his but in the north western side of the place of occurrence house. He (Mozaffar) has a daughter by the name of Jamila, but he was not aware whether she was the first wife of his brother Sultan PW 7. Another wife of Sultan had 3 sons and 2 daughters. On the night of occurrence Sultan was staying with his wife Rina. He further deposed that at the time of occurrence he did not call any of the witnesses and they came there of their own accord. He then deposed that he called Mozahar PW 10. He also deposed that there was a primary school about a mile away from the place of occurrence house and in the middle there were houses of Jagadish, Khitish and Jogesh, but they were not called as witnesses. He deposed that he could not say when Rashid Mondal came to their house. There are 30/32 persons living in that house. One Jatin Master and Pulin Master also lived in that house but none of them appeared as witnesses for the prosecution. Next to their house are the houses of Monoranjan, Naresh Mondal, Haren Basat and Pran Ballab and after their house is located the house of Mominuddin Khan (PW 9). The said PW 9 is the brother of his wife.

11. In cross in reply to a question he said that the Government Primary School is about one mile away to the south and PW 9's house is about 1/4 mile away. In reply to another question he said that after the occurrence he did not go anywhere and stayed at home and his brother Sultan also stayed at home and the only person they called was PW 10. Naren Mondal and Momin Khan came to their house after the occurrence. Chowkidar Khanchan Ali came in the morning. His house is about half a mile away. Shajahan Sowdagar came at 6-00 AM on the next morning. He is a member of the local Union Parishad and lived half a mile away. Shajahan Sowdagor and the accused appellant are of the same family. Accused appellant Khokan's father plies a boat for his living while accused appellant Khairul's father is an Imam of a mosque. On the night of the occurrence his father was not at home. He returned to the but after he went to the police station. His cousin brother Idris went to call his father. Idris is not a witness in the case. He waited for his father until 10-00 AM in the morning and thereafter went to the police station. His father used to live in the same room as the deceased. Next to the father's room was his brother Sultan's room, which was smaller in size. Since it was a small room his children used to sleep with his mother. After the occurrence he went inside the place of occurrence room and found the door on the western side and a window open. In reply to another question he said that she recognised the assailants from the said door. At the time of sleeping the door and window of his father's room are usually locked from inside. He denied that it was not mentioned in the ejahar that the hurricane (lantern) was burning or that the assailants had taken the same away with them. He denied the defence suggestion that at the time of the occurrence the sky was cloudy and that it was raining. He had handed over the Kupi Bati to the police at the time of preparing seizure list and seizing alamat. His mother shouted "Allah" "Allah" which he heard from his room. He went out and saw Sultan. On his mother's bed Kajol, Ripon and Mizan were sleeping. He could not say whether there was any blood on their clothes. There was only one injury on the neck of the deceased. He denied that his mother died then and there when inflicted a blow in her sleep. He denied that his mother was unable to disclose how she was inflicted the injury. He denied the defence suggestion that his mother did not speak to them. He stated that there was bloodstain on his hands. He denied that Kajal, Ripon and Mizan did not see the occurrence. He denied that they did not recognise the assailants. In reply to another question she said that they have five kathas of land, which was cultivated by the accused appellant Khairul for one year. He denied that he would quarrel with his mother for being affectionate to Sultan's children from his first wife. He frankly admitted about previously cultivating the land given to Khairul. He denied that his mother had 4 kathas of land which he wanted to sell and give the sale proceeds to his brother Sultan. In 1986 his mother and sister Rahela were critically injured. He denied the suggestion that he inflicted the injury. He denied the suggestion about filing a false case against Surendra. He denied the defence suggestion that he killed his mother. He denied the implication of his brother Khairul in the instant case for his cultivating his mother's land. He denied the defence suggestion that the accused appellants are not implicated with the offence. He denied the suggestion that he and his wife did not see the accused appellant leaving the place of occurrence with a Dao. He also denied the defence suggestion that he did not wrap his mother's neck with Gamcha. He also denied the defence suggestion that his mother was not alive half an hour after being inflicted with the injury in the neck.

12. PW 4 Kazal Rekha, the daughter of Sultan deposed that she is the daughter by her father's first wife Shefali. After her mother was divorced by her father, her father remarried again and thereafter she used to live with her Dadi (deceased). The relationship between her stepmother and Dadi was not good and frequently there would be quarrels regarding her and her brothers. She deposed that her Dadi was murdered on 10th of Ashar at about 2-00 AM in the night. She along with her brothers were sleeping in her Dadi's room. She deposed that she was awakened by the sound of her Dadi's hue and cry (ডাক চিৎকার). From the light of the hurricane (lantern), she said she saw the accused appellants running away and that there was bleeding injury on the neck of her Dadi. Her Dadi was alive then. Thereafter, her father and uncle came and she saw her Dadi reporting to them that the accused appellants had inflicted the blow on her (Dadi). Thereafter her (Dadi) died. She also deposed that the accused appellant entered the room by a window on the eastern side of the room. The assailants took the lanten away with them. The accused appellant Khairul came to their house in the afternoon prior to the night of occurrence and her stepmother complained to him about her Dadi. She further deposed that she had made her statements to the investigation officer and identified the accused appellants on dock in Court.

13. In cross in reply to a question she said that she along with her brothers were sleeping with their Dadi. Usually in that room she along with her brothers sleep with their Dada and Dadi. Her Dada (deceased's husband) cultivated land belonging to others for a living. Her Dadi's room is comparatively larger. She denied that she used to sleep in her Dadi's room since it was comparatively larger. She denied that her Dadi had given land to the accused appellant for cultivation. She denied the defence suggestion that the informant PW 3 used to break the fencing of his Dadi's but and take away rice from there and for which her Dadi used to scold him. On the night of the occurrence except for her father and uncle no one else came to the place of occurrence house. She admitted that she did not inform the police about seeing the accused appellant leaving the room on the night of the occurrence, as she was not in her senses at that time. She also did not inform the police about the accused appellant taking the hurricane with them. In her Dadi's room the window can be opened and that there are no grills there. The accused appellants had a Dao in their hands, which is used for cutting trees. She saw the injury on her Dadis neck by the light of hurricane. When the accused appellants were leaving, her father and uncle were not inside the place of occurrence room. When her father and uncle entered the place of occurrence room the hurricane was not there. They came with a lamp in their hand. She denied the defence suggestion that her Dadi died in her sleep after sustaining the injury. In reply to a question she said that when her Dadi put her hand round the neck of her father a slight amount of blood fell on them. Her Dadi's bed and clothes were full of her blood. She denied the suggestion that there was no quarrel between her Dadi and her stepmother. She further deposed that her father has two brothers by the name Selim and Delwar. She denied that two of them live in Dhaka due to her father harassing them. She denied the suggestion that she did not see the accused appellant running away from the place of occurrence. She denied the suggestion that there was no quarrel between her stepmother and her Dadi in the afternoon prior to the occurrence. In reply to another question she said that her father married her step-mother 5 years after divorcing her mother. She denied the suggestion that her Dadi was not alive just after the occurrence. She denied about giving false evidence in this case.

14. PW 5 Mizanur Rahman Bulu aged 10 years, son of Sultan (PW 7) deposed similarly to his sister (PW 4) about his father Sultan remarrying after divorcing his mother and that he along with his other brother and sister sleep with their Dadi since they were badly treated by their step-mother. He further deposed that on the night of occurrence ie on the 10th of Ashar he along with Kajal and Ripon were sleeping in their Dadi's room. He was awakened by the mosquito net being cut and he saw two men going away after inflicting a bleeding injury on the left side of his Dadi's neck. He said that he recognised the two persons as the accused appellants and identified them in the dock. The hurricane was burning and he recognised them from its light. The hurricane was taken by the assailants. He further deposed that his Dadi and step-mother used to quarrel very often since his step-mother did not give them food and clothes and that is the reason why the accused appellant killed their Dadi.

15. In cross in reply to a question he said that they often used to give short meals to them. He denied not having told the police that he was awake when the assailants had entered the place of occurrence room. He also denied the defence suggestion that he did not report to the investigation officer about seeing the assailants inflicting the injury on his Dadi. He denied not having told the Investigation officer about recognising the assailants from the light of the hurricane or that the assailants had taken away the hurricane with them. He denied the suggestion that he did not see anything since he was sleeping and that he was giving tutored evidence.

16. PW 6, A Majid Khandker, the husband of the deceased, deposed that his wife was murdered on the 10th of Ashar at about 1:00-1:30 in the night. He said he was away from the place of occurrence house as he was residing at another place about 5/6 miles away. On the following day on receipt of the information from one Idris at about 9-00/9-30 in the morning he went to his homestead and saw his wife dead. He saw his wife's dead body on the bed with her throat cut. There was blood on the bed. His grand-children Kajal and Mizan alias Bu PWs 4 and 5, respectively reported to him that the accused appellants had killed his wife. He came to know from Harun and Sultan (ie PWs 3 and 7) that the deceased had mentioned the names of the accused appellants prior to her death. He also said that (PW 3) had reported to him that he had seen the accused appellants leaving the place of occurrence house after committing the murder. He deposed that his wife used to be affectionate to PW 7's children which was the cause of quarrel between Sultan PW 7's second wife and the deceased, and that is the reason why Sultan's second wife's brother killed the deceased. In cross, he admitted that his brother-in-law Idris is not a witness in the case. In reply to another question he said that he used to sleep on the same bed as the deceased. In reply to another question he said that his wife gave her land to the accused appellant Khairul for cultivation. He denied the defence suggestion that his wife used to like Sultan and his second wife. He denied that there were frequent quarrels between his wife and PW 3 Harun regarding his wife's good relationship with Sultan and his second wife. He denied that his wife had given the land to the accused appellant Khairul against his wishes. He admitted giving the land to the accused appellant Khairul himself on lease. In reply to another question he said that his land was never cultivated by PW 3 Harun and that he did not give any portion of the land to the said PW 3. The deceased used to be very affectionate to the children of PW 7's first wife. He denied the suggestion that PW 3 was angry since property was given to the accused appellant Khairul.

17. In reply to another question he said that he and Harun did not accompany the body to the morgue. His other two sons Delwar and Selim lived in Dhaka and they were not there at the time of occurrence. PW 3 did not consult him prior to the filing of the Ejahar. One Shajahan, a Chowkidar, a member of the Union Parisad and Sultan accompanied PW 3 when he went to file the ejahar. Their ancestral house is Dag No. 62. There are other people's properties also in the same dag number. He denied the suggestion about killing his wife and filing a false case. He denied the suggestion that PW 3 was a man of dangerous character. He denied the suggestion that PW 3 had a grudge against his wife for having given the land to the accused appellant. He denied that his wife owned 4 kathas of land in village Chhitaki which she gave to Sultan and which was a bone of contention with PW 3. He denied the suggestion that PW 3 killed his wife in consultation with him. He denied giving false evidence in the case.

18. PW 7 Sultan Khandker, son of the deceased, deposed that there are three rooms in their homestead and that he along with his second wife stayed in one room. His mother the deceased and his father along with his three children stayed in another room, while in the third room his brother PW 3 used to reside. On the night of the occurrence his father was away from home. At about 2 at night he was awakened by the sound of his mother shouting. When he opened the door he saw his brother PW 3 Harun and his wife. Harun had a light in his hand. In the moonlight as well as by the light in Harun's hand he said he saw the accused appellants running away. Thereafter, he entered his mother's room and found his children crying and his mother's body and clothes were full of blood with bleeding injury on her neck. He wrapped her neck with a Gamcha. His mother “ঘটনা ঘটাইয়াছে” embraced him and his brother and reported to them that the accused appellants Khairul and Khokan had caused the incident “ঘটনা ঘটাইয়াছে” His mother died soon thereafter. His son Mizan and daughter Kajal told him that in the light of the hurricane they recognised the accused appellants. They entered through a window on the eastern side where there is no grill. Both the windows can be opened from outside. He deposed that the accused appellant Khairul is the brother of his wife and accused Khokan is her cousin. He further deposed that his mother and his second wife used to quarrel frequently and that is the reason why the accused appellants have caused the incident. He further deposed that the police during investigation seized the lamp (Kupi Bati), pillow and Gamcha, etc by preparing seizure list where he put his signature as a witness. He proved the seizure list as Exhibit 2 and identified the accused appellants on dock. In cross, in reply to a question he said that he passed the SSC Examination but his brother PW 3 Harun was not much educated. He also said that he was a member of the Ansar and VDP Force in which he used to work in coordination with the police and for that reason he used to maintain communication with the police. In reply to another question he said that he divorced his first wife one-year before he remarried his second wife. In reply to another question he said that he had earlier married PW 10's daughter and had divorced her also. He further stated that at present he is working at Dhaka in a garments factory. He denied the suggestion that on the night of occurrence it was raining. In reply to another question he said that he heard the sound of shouting of his daughter Kajal and son Ripon. He denied the suggestion that there was no hue and cry in the place of occurrence room. He denied the suggestion that PW 3 and his wife called him. He also denied that there was no light in the hand of PW 3. He denied the suggestion that there was no hurricane in the place of occurrence room. He denied the suggestion that he and PW 3 did not see the deceased alive. He admitted that there was only one injury on his mother's neck. He denied the suggestion that his son Mizan and Kajal did not mention the accused appellant's name. He denied the suggestion that PW 3 Harun had killed his mother. He denied the suggestion that his father in alliance with his brother Harun had killed his mother due to a family dispute. He denied the suggestion that there was no quarrel between his second Wife and his mother. His father remarried about one and half years after the occurrence. He denied the suggestion that he was giving false evidence out of fear of his .brother PW 3 Harun. He denied that the accused appellants have been implicated falsely to save PW 3.

19. In cross in reply to a question he said that in the year that the occurrence took place the accused appellant Khairul cultivated 7 (seven) Kuras of land. In reply to another question he said that Khairul had taken 7 Bighas of land for cultivation although PW 3 Harun had his own bullocks for cultivation. In reply to another question he said that Harun never cultivated the said land. At the time of occurrence the children were not wearing any clothes. Some blood fell, on them. He further deposed that PW 3 entered the place of occurrence room before him. When he entered he saw his, mother's blood dripping. In reply to another question he said that the windows of the place of occurrence-room can be locked from inside. His brothers Selim and Delowar came to their homestead after 5/7 days. He denied that there was any quarrel between him and his father and PW 3. He denied that his mother wanted to sell four and a half kathas of land and give him the money. He denied that Harun was angry with his mother because she wanted to give her property as well as the sale proceeds of the land to Sultan. In reply to another question he said that he did not know whether other persons came to the place of occurrence house after the occurrence. In the morning however Shajahan member, A Malek Khan the Chairman of the Union Parisad and others had come there. He denied that he is giving false evidence out of fear. He denied the defence suggestion that he and PW 3 Harun did not recognise the accused appellants.

20. PW 8 Khadija Begum, wife of the informant, deposed that on the night of occurrence she and her husband were awakened from sleep by the sound of hue and cry of Kazal and Mizan and she along with her husband went out of the door and in moonlight as well as with the lamp in her husband's hand saw the accused appellants running away outside the room. They met their brother Sultan. Thereafter they entered their mother's room and saw a bleeding injury on her neck. His mother embraced her husband and his brother and reported to them that the accused appellants had inflicted the injury on her neck. Kazal and Mizan also said that they recognised the accused appellants from the light of the hurricane.

21. In cross she said that she had three sons. In reply to another question, she said that her mother-in-law used to sleep by keeping a lantern burning in her room. When they entered her room they did not see the lantern, as the accused appellants had taken it away. She denied that her husband's mother was not affectionate to her children. In reply to another question she said that she with the informant and her brother-in-law Sultan went inside the deceased's room together and heard the deceased saying "Allah"-"Allah". She denied the suggestion that they did not find her mother-in-law alive at that time.

22. In cross in reply to another question she said that Selim and Delwar came to their house after two days. She denied that she was giving false evidence at the instance of her husband and father-in-law. She denied that the accused appellants were innocent.

23. In reply to a question she said that she was not present during the preparation of the Surathal. After the occurrence the lamp was in the hand of her husband Harun. No one else had any lamp. She denied the suggestion that there was no moonlight on that night. She denied the defence suggestion that she could not recognise any of the accused appellants as reported by her to the police. She denied the defence suggestion that her mother-in-law did not mention the name of the accused appellants to her husband and his brother. She denied the suggestion that she did not tell the investigation officer about the accused appellant taking away the hurricane with them. She denied that she is giving false evidence at the instance of her husband. She denied that she saw her mother-in-law dead.

24. PW 9 Mominuddin Khan deposed that he was known to the informant Harun as well as the accused appellants. His house is about quarter of a mile away from the place of occurrence house. After the occurrence he and Nagen Doctor went to the place of occurrence house and saw the deceased on a bed with bleeding injury on her neck. Sultan and Harun reported to him that the deceased before her death had told them that the accused appellant had inflicted the injury on her. They also told him that they saw the accused appellant by the light of Kupi bati and the moonlight. The police had seized Alamat in his presence and that he had signed the seizure list. He proved the seizure list as Exhibit 3 and his signature as Exhibit 3/1. Blood-stained saree, blood-stained pillow, blood-stained Gamcha and mosquito net and thin bamboo mat were seized by the police.

25. In cross he stated that Harun's wife Khadiza is his cousin sister and the chairman of the Union Parisad A Malek Khan is his brother. In reply to another question he said that just after the occurrence it was raining. He, however, deposed that there was no rain after the occurrence. In reply to another question he said that PW 3 Harun went to his house at about 2 at night. He denied the defence suggestion that Harun did not visit his house on the night of the occurrence or that he did not got to the place of occurrence house the same night. He denied the suggestion that Sultan did not tell him that the deceased had told him that the accused appellant had killed her. He denied the defence suggestion that he was giving false evidence in this case.

26. In reply to another question he said that he did not see any blood on the person of Harun. In reply to another question he said that Nagen was called first by Harun. At the place of occurrence house he saw Mozhar and clotted blood on the body. There was no other outsider at that time. Mozahar did not tell them anything.

27. PW 10 Mozafar Ali alias Mozahar Ali deposed that the informant Harun is known to him. On the night of the occurrence he went to the place of occurrence house and saw hue and cry there and that Suratan Bibi was lying dead with bleeding injury on her neck. Her bedding and clothes were full of blood. On his asking it was reported to him by Sultan and Harun that the accused appellants had killed her and fled away. The deceased had also told to Sultan and Harun that the accused appellants had inflicted the injury on her. In reply to another question he said that Sultan used to be married to his daughter but divorced her 10 years ago.

28. In cross in reply to a question he said that his homestead was 2/3 minutes away and that he went to the place of occurrence house on hearing the shout of Sultan and Harun. He was at the place of occurrence until morning. In reply to another question he said that after going there Harun went to call Momin. In reply to another question he said that it was a moonlit night then and that Nagen Mondal also went there. He denied that he has given false evidence in this case. In reply to another question he said that he saw the Kupi bati next to the deceased. He saw the children of Sultan crying in the same bed as the deceased but there was no blood on their clothes. In the year of the occurrence the accused appellants Khairu and Khokan were cultivating the deceased land. The two other sons of the deceased came to their home three or four days after occurrence. In reply to another question he said, that he was not aware as to whether the accused appellants were innocent. He denied that he is giving false evidence in the case.

29. PW 11 Nagen Mondal was tendered by the prosecution. In cross in reply to a question he said that he was called to the place of occurrence house on the night of the occurrence by Harun PW 3. In reply to another question he said that he went to the place of occurrence house when it was almost morning. At the place of occurrence house he saw Mozahar (PW 10) and 4/5 others.

30. PW 12 Md Monwar Hossain, Investigation officer of the case, deposed about his investigation. He deposed that on 26-6-91 ejahar was lodged by the informant Harun at Kathalia PS and he registered the case after completing the necessary formalities. He proved the ejahar as Ext 1. He deposed about visiting the place of occurrence, arranging the post mortem examination on the body of the deceased, preparing surathal report, preparing sketch map of the place of occurrence with separate index, seizing alamats and taking statements from witnesses and thereafter submitted charge-sheet against the accused appellants. In cross in reply to a question he said that on 26-6-91 he prepared a seizure list being Exhibit 3. On the following day on 27-6-91 he prepared another seizure list being Exhibit 2. In reply to another question he said that a mark of injury came to his attention while preparing Surathal report. However, there is no mention in the said report about finding evidence of any wrapping at the place of injury. In reply to another question he said that there is no mention of seizure list as Exhibit 2 in the case diary. In reply to another question he said that the doctor could not give any opinion as to whether the deceased could speak or was able to speak after being inflicted with the injury. In reply to another question he said that there is no mention of Kupi bati and there is no mention of recognition of the kupi bati in the ejahar. In reply to another question he said that Kazal, Ripon and Mizan did not report to him about the recognition of the accused appellants. They also did not report to him about the hurricane burning at the time of occurrence at the place of occurrence room. In fact, he stated that at the time of occurrence Mijan, Ripon and Kazal were sleeping as reported by them and that they were awakened by hearing the sound of groaning by the deceased.

31. In reply to another question he said that there is no mention in the ejahar about the neck of the deceased being wrapped by Gamcha. There is no mention regarding quarrel on the previous day in the ejahar. In reply to another question he said that he did not examine Selim and Delowar.

32. PW 13, Dr Md Akhtaruzzaman, deposed that on 27-6-91 while he was at Jhalokati Sadar Hospital as RMO he conducted the post mortem examination of the deceased and found the following injuries:

Anterior aspect of neck from left submodifular angle to 2 left to right submodifular angle transversely measuring about 8" x 2" x 2" (Trachea, vessels, muscles and skin and nerve cut).

33. In his opinion, the death was caused by excessive bleeding. He proved the post mortem report. In cross in reply to a, question he said that he was not aware as to whether the Investigation officer had asked him as to whether the deceased was able to speak after being inflicted with the injury. In reply to another question he said that after being inflicted with the aforesaid injury the deceased could or could not, may or may not die in her sleep, but that she would be awakened from her sleep in view of the injury.

34. This is for the evidence on record.

35. It appears that there is no eye-witness to the occurrence. None saw who had killed the deceased. The trial Court, however, convicted the accused appellants on the basis of the evidence by PWs 3, 7, 8 and children of PW 7'S first wife, PW 4 and 5. In the else of Shafiullah alias Kale Min vs State reported in 1985 BLD 129 His Lordship Mr Justice ATM Afzal has said that to warrant a conviction on circumstantial evidence, the evidence must satisfy three tests (i) circumstances from which an inference of guilt is sought to be drawn, must be cogently and firmly established; (ii) those circumstances should be of a definite tendency unerringly pointing towards the guilt of the accused, (iii) the circumstances,, taken cumulatively, should form a chain so complete that there is no escape from the conclusion that within all human probability the crime was committed by the accused and none else. The circumstantial evidence in order to sustain a conviction must be complete and incapable of explanation on any other hypothesis than that of the guilt of the accused. It must be qualitatively such that on every reasonable hypothesis the conclusion must be that the accused is guilty, not fantastic possibilities nor freak inferences. But rational deduction which reasonable minds make from the probative force of facts and circumstances."

<u>36. In the instant case the trial Court convicted the accused appellants on the basis of evidence adduced by PWs 3, 7, 8 and children of PW 7's first wife, PWs 4 and 5. The informant, PW 2 in his deposition clearly stated that when he entered into the place of occurrence room, PW 7's children PWs 4 and 5 were sleeping. However, the said PWs 4 and 5 deposed that they had seen the accused appellants inflicting the injury upon the deceased. Furthermore, PWs 4 and 5 did not state to the Investigating Officer at the earliest opportunity about seeing the occurrence personally in their statements under section 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. The evidence of PWs 4 and 5, therefore, is not at all believable and is clearly an after thought and designed to prove the case against the accused appellants by way of embellishment.</u>

<u>37. Now comes the matter of absence of independent and disinterested witnesses in this case. In the instant case all the prosecution witnesses appeared to be related to each other. Witnesses from amongst the neighbours were not examined by the prosecution. Non examination of independent and relevant witnesses goes against the prosecution and creates presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act and creates a doubt upon the prosecution case and it is to be presumed that had they been examined by the prosecution they would not have supported the prosecution case. Thus the benefit of this defect will go in favour of the defence.</u>

<u>38. The next point to note is that the motive of killing the deceased, as claimed by the prosecution, is due to the deceased having quarrel with PW 7's second wife regarding the children by PW 7's first wife, and also the allegation that PW 7's second wife reported the incident of a quarrel to her brother, the accused appellant No. 1 and her cousin, whereupon the accused appellant No. 2 allegedly became enraged and subsequently killed the deceased. In such a situation it is difficult to understand why PW 7's second wife, the person around whom the motive for the killing of the deceased centered, was not made a party in the proceedings either as an accused or a prosecution witness. This again, makes the prosecution case highly suspicious and the inference about the accused appellants guilt goes in favour of the defence.</u>

<u>39. Then comes the question as to why no blood was spilled on the children who were sleeping next to the deceased. When the throat of the deceased was cut by the infliction of a single blow with a weapon blood was bound to have gushed out and in the process some blood spilled on those sleeping next to the deceased. In the present case however, no blood was spilled on any of the children as confirmed by PWs 4 and 5. This again, casts doubt on the prosecution case as to the place of occurrence ie as to whether, in fact, the deceased was killed while sleeping in her bed as alleged or somewhere else and her dead body placed on the bed subsequently.</u>

<u>40. Finally, it is not clear why the prosecution did not clarify from the doctor who deposed in court and who conducted the post mortem examination on the deceased, as to whether it was possible for the informant's mother to make any statement by way of dying declaration as alleged by the prosecution after sustaining injury prior to her death. Not having adduced this important evidence despite the Suggestion from the defence to the effect that death was instantaneous after sustaining injury, must also go against the prosecution for not having fulfilled its burden of proving its case beyond reasonable doubt.</u>

<u>41. In a case of circumstantial evidence, such as the present one, the above mentioned facts and circumstances, assume paramount importance and by taking all the evidence cumulatively it cannot be said that the guilt of the accused appellants have been proved beyond a shadow of doubt, and accordingly, we are of the opinion that this appeal has substance and that the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.</u>

42. This appeal is thus allowed. The impugned order of conviction and sentence dated 18-5-95 passed by the Sessions Judge, Jhalokati in Sessions Case No. 11 of 1993 is hereby set aside and the accused appellants Khairul @ Abul Kalam Sawdagor and Khokon Sawdagor be set at liberty forthwith, if they are not wanted in any other case.

Send down the lower court records along with a copy of the judgment at once to the trial Court concerned for necessary information and action.
